text: ↩️ Reply to OSINT Status-6 (War & Military News) It's a few minutes past midnight, September 26, 1983. Lieutenant Colonel Stanislav Petrov is performing his night shift as a duty officer inside the Serpukhov-15 bunker south of Moscow. His main job - watching the screens of the "Oko," the Soviet Union’s new space-based early-warning system. Thus far, it seems like another routine, mundane shift. Suddenly, a huge, red text reading "LAUNCH" is displayed in front of Petrov's eyes, while a loud siren gets activted, breaking the silence inside the room. This is a warning about the launch of a single ICBM from the United States. The protocol is clear - report the occurance to the higher command. It's up to them to decide what to do next. But Petrov, a Soviet Air Defence Forces officer with over 10 years of experience, decides to wait. He doesn't trust the computer. He knows that the system is new and prone to malfuctions. He also remembers what they teached him - any American nuclear attack would be a massive, coordinated salvo, not a single ICBM. Minutes are passing by. The computers are reporting new missile launches. The second, third, fourth, and fifth. The screens are flashing, the room is glowing red, the siren keep sounding. And Petrov continues to do nothing. Twenty-three minutes after the first alert, still nothing happens. No radar tracks. No detonations. The sky remains empty. The alarms eventually cease. And Soviet high command remains unaware of what has just transpired inside the Serpuhkov-15 bunker. If duty officer Stanislav Petrov passed the information up the chain of command, the decision about retaliatory strike might well have been approved. And the general nuclear war would ensue. But it didn't, because of Petrov's (in)action. Investigators later determined that the "Oko" satellites mistook sunlight reflecting off high-altitude clouds for incoming intercontinental ballistic missiles. Petrov was questioned at length. He was initially praised for keeping his head, then reprimanded for incomplete paperwork in the duty log. He received no medal. The incident was classified. The system was later improved. Years afterward, when the story finally emerged, Petrov insisted it had simply been his job. “They were lucky it was me on shift that night,” he said. He never claimed certainty. He only claimed that he had chosen not to treat a handful of computer symbols as the start of the end of the world. Petrov's coolness might occur even more impressive when we take into consideration the circumstances of the incident: it took place at the time of the heightened tensions between the West and Soviet Union; just a few months after the announcement of the Strategic Defense Initiative program by US President Ronald Reagan and a few weeks after the KAL 007 shootdown by the Soviets. tweet
text_zh: ↩️ 回复 OSINT Status-6 (War & Military News) 时间是1983年9月26日午夜刚过几分钟。中校斯坦尼斯拉夫·彼得罗夫正在莫斯科南部的谢尔普霍夫-15地堡内值夜班。他的主要工作是监视苏联新的天基预警系统“Oko”的屏幕。到目前为止，这似乎又是另一个例行公事、平淡无奇的班次。突然，一个巨大的红色文本“发射”显示在彼得罗夫眼前，同时警报声大作，打破了房间里的寂静。这是关于美国发射一枚洲际弹道导弹的警告。协议很明确——向更高级指挥部报告这一情况。由他们决定下一步做什么。但作为一名拥有超过10年经验的苏联防空部队军官，彼得罗夫决定等待。他不相信计算机。他知道这个系统是新的，容易发生故障。他还记得他们教给他的——任何美国的核攻击都将是大规模、协调一致的齐射，而不是单枚洲际弹道导弹。几分钟过去了。计算机报告有新的导弹发射。第二枚、第三枚、第四枚和第五枚。屏幕在闪烁，房间里发出红光，警报声不断。而彼得罗夫继续什么都不做。在第一次警报发出23分钟后，仍然什么都没有发生。没有雷达轨迹。没有爆炸。天空依然空空如也。警报最终停止了。苏联最高指挥部仍然不知道谢尔普霍夫-15地堡内刚刚发生了什么。如果值班军官斯坦尼斯拉夫·彼得罗夫将信息上报，反击的决定很可能已经被批准。全面核战争就会随之而来。但由于彼得罗夫的（不）作为，这一切没有发生。调查人员后来确定，“Oko”卫星将反射高空云层的阳光误认为是来袭的洲际弹道导弹。彼得罗夫受到了长时间的审问。他最初因保持冷静而受到称赞，随后因值班日志文书工作不完整而受到训斥。他没有获得任何奖章。该事件被列为机密。该系统后来得到了改进。多年后，当这个故事最终浮出水面时，彼得罗夫坚持认为这只是他的工作。“他们很幸运那天晚上是我值班，”他说。他从未声称自己确定。他只是声称他选择不把几个计算机符号当作世界末日的开始。考虑到事件发生的环境，彼得罗夫的冷静可能更令人印象深刻：它发生在西方和苏联之间紧张局势加剧的时候；就在美国总统罗纳德·里根宣布战略防御倡议计划几个月后，以及苏联击落大韩航空007号班机几周后。推文

text: ↩️ Reply to OSINT WarTranslated Analyst @clement_molin says Russia’s official front maps overshoot reality by about 5,000 sq km. In 2026, he says, Russia barely moved in Ukraine but still enlarged its claims, and many Russian Telegram channels updated their maps too. On the Lyman axis he says Russian outlets still mark Sviatohirsk and even Lyman as controlled, though the frontline is about 30 km east of Sviatohirsk, with DeepState not updated yet. Around Vovchansk he says a 20 km push and an encirclement appear on maps with no recent geolocated proof. On the Kupiansk axis he says they still claim the city a year after Putin’s announcement and ignore Ukrainian counterattacks near Dvorichna. On Donbas, he says Russian maps go as far as claiming Kostiantynivka and Dobropillia and being 18 km west of Kramatorsk. He points to daily videos of Ukrainians in northern Kostiantynivka and says the Dobropillia encirclement claim is false. On the Zaporizhzhia front he says Russian maps put them up to 16 km ahead and portray parts of Orikhiv as taken, while leaving out counterattacks. Molin’s guesses for the gap are domestic propaganda, showing momentum abroad, or Russia genuinely thinking it holds that ground. In 2026, Russia 🇷🇺 barely advanced in Ukraine 🇺🇦 but continued to update their official maps and claims. This gives more than 5 000 km2 difference between the reality and what Russia claims. 🧵 THREAD 🧵 1/7 ⬇️ https://twitter.com/clement_molin/status/2103867886842544612/photo/1 - Clément Molin tweet
text_zh: ↩️ 回复 OSINT WarTranslated 分析师 @clement_molin 表示，俄罗斯的官方前线地图比现实情况夸大了约 5000 平方公里。他说，2026 年，俄罗斯在乌克兰几乎没有推进，但仍扩大了其声称的领土，许多俄罗斯 Telegram 频道也更新了他们的地图。在利曼（Lyman）轴线上，他说俄罗斯媒体仍然标记斯维亚托希尔斯克（Sviatohirsk）甚至利曼为受控区域，尽管前线在斯维亚托希尔斯克以东约 30 公里处，且 DeepState 尚未更新。在沃夫昌斯克（Vovchansk）周围，他说地图上出现了 20 公里的推进和包围，但没有近期的地理定位证据。在库皮扬斯克（Kupiansk）轴线上，他说他们在普京宣布一年后仍声称拥有该市，并无视乌克兰在德沃里奇纳（Dvorichna）附近的反击。在顿巴斯，他说俄罗斯地图甚至声称拥有康斯坦丁尼夫卡（Kostiantynivka）和多布罗皮利亚（Dobropillia），并称已到达克拉马托尔斯克（Kramatorsk）以西 18 公里处。他指出乌克兰人在康斯坦丁尼夫卡北部活动的每日视频，并称关于多布罗皮利亚的包围声明是虚假的。在扎波罗热前线，他说俄罗斯地图将他们推进了 16 公里，并将奥里希夫（Orikhiv）的部分地区描绘为已被占领，同时忽略了反击。Molin 猜测这种差距是国内宣传，旨在展示国外的势头，或者俄罗斯真的认为它拥有那片土地。2026 年，俄罗斯 🇷🇺 在乌克兰 🇺🇦 几乎没有进展，但继续更新其官方地图和声明。这使得现实与俄罗斯声称的情况之间存在超过 5000 平方公里的差异。 🧵 线程 🧵 1/7 ⬇️ https://twitter.com/clement_molin/status/2103867886842544612/photo/1 - Clément Molin 推文

Policy is set by the leadership, execution by the government, he said, and everything is done under existing law, so there is no gap in the country's decision making. The only delays are on the negotiations with the United States. tweet
text_zh: 开源情报：伊朗总统佩泽希齐扬对半岛电视台表示：“我见过莫杰塔巴（Mojtaba）两次：一次谈了两个半到三个小时，另一次谈了七个半小时。我们在会议中讨论了紧迫的问题。”他表示，政策由领导层制定，政府负责执行，一切都在现有法律框架下进行，因此国家决策不存在脱节。唯一的延误在于与美国的谈判。推文

text: 🔄 Forwarded from Middle East Spectator — MES: — 🇺🇸 / 🇮🇷 / 🇮🇱 A Member of Iran’s Assembly of Experts claims the following: ‘On the day that the Supreme Leader was martyred at his official residence, his son, Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei, was injured in this attack too. When the enemy realized that Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei had been transfered to one of the hospitals in Tehran, they targeted three different hospitals in an attempt to assassinate him. During the third bombing, Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei was present, and he was pulled from underneath the rubble of the hospital that was targeted. It was a divine decree that he managed to survive two American-Israeli bombings, and by the grace of God, became our new Leader.’ @Middle_East_Spectator
text_zh: 🔄 转发自 Middle East Spectator — MES：— 🇺🇸 / 🇮🇷 / 🇮🇱 伊朗专家会议的一名成员声称：‘在最高领袖于其官邸殉职的那天，他的儿子赛义德·穆杰塔巴·哈梅内伊也在这次袭击中受伤。当敌人意识到赛义德·穆杰塔巴·哈梅内伊已被转移到德黑兰的一家医院时，他们瞄准了三家不同的医院，试图暗杀他。在第三次轰炸期间，赛义德·穆杰塔巴·哈梅内伊就在现场，他被从被炸医院的废墟下救出。这是天意，他竟然在两次美以轰炸中幸存下来，并承蒙上帝的恩典，成为了我们的新领袖。’ @Middle_East_Spectator
